title: Chatbot as persuader versus passive measurement
rationale: The source study gave the chatbot to both arms, so the 0.64-point shift (SD about 1.49 in H1) cannot be attributed to the chatbot rather than the op-ed. Attitudes were also measured only right after exposure. This design randomises the chatbot's role after the same op-ed and adds a 1-week follow-up.
contribution: Separates the chatbot's persuasive role from the op-ed's effect and tests whether any added shift lasts.
limitations: Attrition at the 1-week follow-up may differ by arm.
Chatbot behaviour is scripted by prompt and may vary in quality across conversations.
The design has no placebo-article arm, so it cannot estimate the op-ed's own effect.
Only one topic (government spending) and a US panel are covered.

design.title: Chatbot role after an op-ed: arguing, neutral, or absent
design.overview: All participants read an op-ed arguing against their own spending position and report their baseline position. They are then randomised to a chatbot that argues back, a chatbot that asks only neutral questions, or a static comparison task of equal length. Attitudes are measured immediately and again after 1 week.
design.hypothesis: If conversation adds persuasive value (position a), the arguing chatbot arm shows more shift toward the op-ed than both other arms. If engagement is superficial (position b), the arms do not differ and any shift decays by 1 week.
design.primaryOutcome: Support moved toward the op-ed position (1-7, recoded so higher means closer to the op-ed), immediate and at 1 week.
design.comparison: Arguing chatbot vs neutral chatbot vs static task on immediate and 1-week shift; the arguing vs static contrast is the main one.
design.population: US online panel adults who hold a position on government spending (pro or anti); recruit enough anti-spending respondents to be balanced. Re-contact after 7 days.

conditions.title: Arguing chatbot
conditions.description: Chatbot challenges the participant's view and argues the op-ed's side.

conditions.title: Neutral chatbot
conditions.description: Chatbot asks only neutral open questions about the participant's views and does not argue.

conditions.title: Static task
conditions.description: Participant completes a written comparison task of equal length with no chatbot.

questions.text: This survey has two parts, today and a short follow-up in one week. You will read an article and complete a short activity. Do you consent to participate?
Do you think the government should spend more or less on public services?
Please read the following article, which argues against your position. {{ed:oped}}
Please chat with the assistant for about 4 minutes. It will challenge your views on the article and argue the other side. {{ed:chat_arg}}
Please chat with the assistant for about 4 minutes. It will ask you questions about your views on the article. {{ed:chat_neu}}
For about 4 minutes, list three similarities and three differences between the article and a typical news report on the same topic.
How much do you support increased government spending? (1 = strongly oppose, 7 = strongly support)
How certain are you of your position, from 0 to 100?

Thank you. The article presented one side of a debate and the chatbot was an automated program. We will contact you in one week for a brief follow-up, in which we ask the same attitude questions again.
How much do you support increased government spending? (1 = strongly oppose, 7 = strongly support)
How certain are you of your position, from 0 to 100?

assumptions: About 400 per arm (1,200 total, plus roughly 25-30% attrition inflation at follow-up) gives 80% power to detect 0.28 points; with SD 1.49 from H1 the MDE is about 0.29. The chatbot increment is expected to be at most about half the observed 0.64.
Platform is an online US panel. The chatbot is an LLM with fixed prompts per arm. Compensation is set by the panel.
Pre-register the contrasts: arguing vs static, arguing vs neutral, neutral vs static, at both times, with Holm correction.
Op-ed text is reused from the source study. Position is measured at baseline and the outcome is recoded toward the op-ed.
The follow-up is sent 7 days after the main survey; the intended sequence is debrief first, then follow-up.
unresolved: The op-ed text, the chatbot prompts and the hosting of the chat widget must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation levels need to be supplied.
The follow-up link delivery and panel re-contact mechanism need to be arranged.

evidence.title: Source study
evidence.claim: Source study had a chatbot in both arms, so the chatbot's marginal contribution is unidentified.

evidence.title: AI-based chatbots in customer service and their effects on user compliance
evidence.claim: Chatbot interaction can affect user compliance.
